name: Swiss roll
origin: Despite the name, likely not Swiss in origin; a thin, fatless whisked sponge baked as a sheet, spread with jam or cream while still warm and pliable, then rolled into a spiral and left to cool in that shape.

ingredients.note: an especially egg-rich, fat-free whisked sponge — the high egg content and thin sheet are what let it roll without cracking

process.name: whip eggs and sugar
process.description: whip whole eggs and sugar to full ribbon-stage volume

process.name: fold in flour
process.description: fold in sifted flour gently, preserving as much of the whipped air as possible

process.name: spread thin and bake
process.description: spread thinly on a lined sheet pan and bake hot and fast, so the thin layer sets before it dries out

process.name: roll while warm
process.description: turn out onto sugared paper, spread with jam or cream, and roll into a spiral while still warm and pliable

notes: No added fat at all, real and correctly modelled as zero — a Swiss roll's sheet has to stay pliable enough to roll without cracking, and added fat would work against that. Tagged 'tunnel': like lamington, a thin standardised sheet sponge is a real candidate for continuous-belt commercial baking. The jam or cream filling is a separately-prepared component spread on after baking, out of scope for this batter's formulation.
